cultural.summary: No specific local HP practice is documented yet for late blight.
cultural.how: Consult local elders or use the classical Vrikshayurveda treatments below.

biological.summary: Give stressed potato plants a soothing licorice-honey drink to help them fight off cold wet rot!
biological.how: Prepare a decoction of Yashtimadhu (licorice root) and Madhuca, mixed with milk and honey. Irrigate the affected plant.

biological.summary: Wrap the sick plant in a gentle honey-ghee smoke to calm the stress before it spreads!
biological.how: Fumigate the affected area with honey and ghee.

cultural.summary: Himachal farmers have been dusting ash around plants for generations—simple, cheap, and it works!
cultural.how: Dust wood ash around the base of the plant.

biological.summary: A traditional cow-dung mix that local farmers trust as a natural plant protector!
biological.how: Mix cow dung into a natural pesticide preparation and apply to the plant/soil.

biological.summary: The same soothing licorice-honey drink also helps calm yellowing, sun-stressed leaves!
biological.how: Prepare a decoction of Yashtimadhu (licorice root) and Madhuca, mixed with milk and honey. Irrigate.

cultural.summary: Vrikshayurveda centers on trees and leaves; it doesn't have a clear category for tuber-skin conditions.
cultural.how: No HP-specific documented local practice found. Flagged for farmer interviews.

cultural.summary: No specific local HP practice is documented yet for bacterial wilt.
cultural.how: Consult local elders or use the classical Vrikshayurveda treatments below.

biological.summary: The same calming licorice-honey drink used for stressed, sun-struggling plants!
biological.how: Prepare a decoction of Yashtimadhu (licorice root) and Madhuca, mixed with milk and honey. Irrigate.

cultural.summary: Tuck neem cake into the soil to give roots a protective, worm-unfriendly bed!
cultural.how: Mix neem cake into the soil before planting.
cultural.frequency: Once at planting, refresh every 2-3 months

cultural.summary: Plant cheerful marigolds nearby—their roots naturally shoo pesky nematodes away!
cultural.how: Plant marigold near or before the potato crop.

biological.summary: A week of cool water baths helps calm irritated, wiggly-worm-troubled roots!
biological.how: Irrigate the plant with cold water for seven consecutive days.

biological.summary: A gentle homemade paste tucked right at the roots to soothe worm troubles!
biological.how: Apply a paste of cow dung, water, and milk to the affected root area.

biological.summary: A zesty herbal paste that gives pesky root worms a reason to move along!
biological.how: Combine white mustard, Vacha (sweet flag), and Kushta into a paste. Apply directly to the affected part.

cultural.summary: Tuck fragrant local leaves in with stored potatoes to keep hungry moths away all season!
cultural.how: Layer leaves of Lantana, Eupatorium, and Eucalyptus in with or around stored potato tubers.
cultural.frequency: At storage time, refresh as leaves dry out
